title: Which kind of wizard would you be?
topic: Which kind of wizard would you be
intro: Nine questions about libraries, village fairs and spells gone slightly wrong. Dust off your hat and find out what sort of magic you'd practise.

outcomes.name: Storm Caller
outcomes.tagline: Big gestures, bright sparks and a cape that's always flapping.
outcomes.description: Your magic is loud, bold and best watched from a safe distance. You leap first and work out the landing on the way down, and somehow it usually works. People feel braver standing next to you, and nobody ever forgets the day you turned up.

outcomes.name: Hedge Wizard
outcomes.tagline: Herbs on the windowsill, soup on the stove, a cure for everything.
outcomes.description: Your magic is the everyday kind that actually helps: a balm for a scraped knee, a tea for a bad night, a garden that feeds the whole lane. You're steady and practical, and your kitchen is where everyone ends up when they need looking after.

outcomes.name: Stargazer
outcomes.tagline: Up the tallest tower, reading tomorrow in the sky.
outcomes.description: You see patterns other people miss and you're happiest with a quiet night and a big question. Friends come to you for perspective, because you always seem to be looking a little further ahead. Your notebooks are full of dreams, maps and very good hunches.

outcomes.name: Enchanter
outcomes.tagline: One smile, one sparkle, and the whole room is on your side.
outcomes.description: Your magic works on people, and you use it for good: soothing arguments, starting parties and making strangers feel like old friends. You know exactly the right word at the right moment. Half your spells are just charm, and honestly that's the best half.

outcomes.name: Alchemist
outcomes.tagline: Scorch marks on the ceiling, a breakthrough in the notebook.
outcomes.description: You want to know how everything works, and then you want to make it work better. You're patient with experiments and impatient with 'because that's how it's done'. Your workshop is a glorious mess of bubbling jars, and every failure is just data.

outcomes.name: Beast Keeper
outcomes.tagline: Owls on your shoulder, foxes at your door, friends with everything.
outcomes.description: Your magic is mostly listening, and every creature in the forest seems to know it. You're gentle, observant and fiercely loyal to the ones you love, whether they have two legs, four or wings. Wherever you settle, something small and furry moves in.

questions.text: You're let loose in an ancient library. Which shelf do you reach for first?

answers.text: Old charts of the night sky
Battered cookbooks full of margin notes
Notebooks from failed experiments
Field guides to forest birds
Bundles of old love letters
Accounts of famous shipwrecks

questions.text: Someone knocks on your door at midnight. You…

answers.text: Fling it open, whoever it is
Put the kettle on, then answer
Guess who it is before you look
Open it with a grin and a joke
Ask a trick question through the door
Wait to see if the cat hisses

questions.text: Your wizard's home has one unusual feature. It's…

answers.text: A balcony right above the sea
A greenhouse inside the kitchen
An attic with a glass roof
A ballroom you could never fill
A workshop with a scorched ceiling
A porch built into a tree

questions.text: A spell goes wrong and turns your eyebrows blue. You…

answers.text: Show them off at a party
Work out exactly what went wrong
Try the spell again, but bigger
Mix up a remedy and fix it
Take it as a sign of something
Ask your owl if it noticed

questions.text: Which job at the village fair is yours?

answers.text: Reading fortunes in a little tent
Judging the jam competition
Setting off the fireworks
Hosting the talent show
Fixing the broken carousel
Running the petting zoo

questions.text: What gets you out of bed on a cold morning?

answers.text: The smell of something baking
Wild weather I don't want to miss
A half-finished idea
A pet waiting for breakfast
Plans with people I like
A dream I want to write down
Dive straight in
Read the instructions first
Watch someone else try first

questions.text: You find a dusty old chest. Inside is…

answers.text: A brass telescope
A pouch of ancient seeds
A cloak that catches the wind
A ring that makes strangers smile
A box of unlabelled bottles
A whistle only animals can hear

questions.text: A friend wants help asking someone out. You…

answers.text: Write them a dazzling speech
Make them a calming cup of tea
Tell them to go for it tonight
Research their favourite things
Suggest a walk in the woods
Help them pick the perfect moment
